title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page continues a verification begun on the previous page. A profinite group (written \hat{S}^+ on the previous page, \mathfrak{G}_4^+ here) is presented by generators \rho, \sigma with relations \rho^6=\sigma^4=1, \rho^3=\sigma^2=:\omega (central, of order 2) and [\sigma,\lambda_\infty]=1, where \lambda_\infty=\rho\sigma\rho^{-1}\sigma\rho. This is an SL(2,Z)-type amalgam (Z/6 *_{Z/2} Z/4) with an extra commutation relation. M is an abelian normal piece, written multiplicatively or additively, with generators \lambda_0 and \lambda_1=\rho(\lambda_0); also \sigma(\lambda_0)=\lambda_1. On M the conjugation actions satisfy \rho_M^3=\sigma_M^2=id_M and 1+\rho_M+\rho_M^2=0. So M is a rank-2 module on which \rho acts as an order-3 rotation; it is essentially the G_0 of the next page.

Goal. Grothendieck wants, for a 'multiplier' \mu, a homomorphism u from \mathfrak{G}_4^+ to the group of S_0-points \underline{\mathfrak{G}}_4^+(S_0). It is defined by twisting the generators by elements of M:
- \rho' = \zeta\rho;
- \sigma' = \eta_0\,\omega^{\nu_2}\sigma, with \nu_2 \in \{0,1\};
- \zeta = \alpha_0-\rho(\alpha_0)+\xi\lambda_1 and \eta_0 = \beta_0-\sigma(\beta_0) (from (45)).
The map should satisfy u(\lambda)=\mu\lambda on M ((41), (42)). The previous page reduces everything to two checks: (47) \rho'^3=\sigma'^2=\omega, and (49) \lambda'_\infty=\mu\lambda_\infty.

This page.
1. It notes that (49) follows once (47) holds.
2. It computes \rho'^3=\zeta\rho(\zeta)\rho^2(\zeta)\,\omega and \sigma'^2=\eta_0\sigma(\eta_0)\,\omega. The factor \omega^{2\nu_2}=1 because \omega is central of order 2.
3. So (47) reduces to the norm conditions (50): N_\rho(\zeta)=1 and N_\sigma(\eta_0)=1. Additively these read \zeta+\rho\zeta+\rho^2\zeta=0 and \eta_0+\sigma\eta_0=0.
4. These are the standard conditions for a twisted generator g\cdot t, with t a finite-order generator and g in an abelian normal subgroup, to keep the order of t, i.e. 1-cocycle conditions for a cyclic group.
   - The first holds trivially because 1+\rho_M+\rho_M^2=0 on all of M.
   - The second holds because \eta_0=(1-\sigma)\beta_0 and (1+\sigma)(1-\sigma)=1-\sigma^2=0.
5. Hence the homomorphism u: \mathfrak{G}_4^+ \to \underline{\mathfrak{G}}_4^+(S_0) exists. It remains to check (41) and (42).
6. For (41) he sets u(\lambda_0)=\mu\lambda_0 and u(\lambda_1)=\mu\lambda_1. He starts recomputing 'pour être sûr' the image of \varepsilon_0=\sigma\rho: \varepsilon_0' = \eta_0\omega^{\nu_2}\sigma\zeta\rho = \eta_0\,\sigma(\zeta)\,\omega^{\nu_2}\,\varepsilon_0.
7. The next page finishes the check: it reduces \varepsilon_0'=\varepsilon_0^{(\mu)} to \xi=\eta_0+\nu\lambda_1, true by hypothesis (31). It then assembles the scheme/groupoid \tilde Z_{\rho,\sigma} over S_0, with maps \nu' to G_0 and \nu_2 to \{0,1\}, and \mu=4\nu'+2+\nu_2.

Purpose. This is a hands-on construction of the automorphisms ('anchorings') of an SL_2-type extension that act by a scalar \mu on the abelian part. They are parametrized by a twisted-constant scheme of choices. It is part of the Longue Marche programme of describing explicitly, in genus 1 / level structures, the Teichmüller-type groups and their Galois/\hat{Z}^*-type symmetries.
errors: The written justification of \eta_0+\sigma(\eta_0)=0 cites only \sigma_M^2=id. In fact one needs \eta_0 to lie in the image of 1-\sigma (as in (45), \eta_0=\beta_0-\sigma(\beta_0)); \sigma^2=id alone does not imply it. This is implicit, not a real gap.

The computation of \sigma'^2 silently drops the factor \omega^{\nu_2}. This is legitimate only because \omega is central of order 2, so \omega^{2\nu_2}=1. On the previous page \sigma' is sometimes written without this factor (u(\sigma)=y_0\sigma), a notational inconsistency.
Notation drifts between \zeta and \xi (and x, y, y_0, \eta_0) across pages for the same twisting elements.

ideas.what: Defining a homomorphism out of a presented group (amalgam of finite cyclic groups plus a commutation relation) by twisting the generators by elements of an abelian normal subgroup. The relation-preservation reduces to norm conditions N_\rho(\zeta)=1, N_\sigma(\eta)=1.
ideas.modern_name: 1-cocycle / norm condition for cyclic groups; twisting finite-order generators; H^1(Z/n, M)

ideas.modern_name: explicit genus-1 / M_{1,1}-type outer actions of \hat{Z}^* (Galois/GT-type actions on profinite SL_2(Z) and its extensions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse programme); later Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto, Enriquez (elliptic GT) for genus-1 Galois actions
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981), circulated partially; the specific construction is apparently only in these notes

missed.claim: This page is only a routine verification step (norm conditions), but it belongs to an explicit, scheme-theoretic parametrization (\tilde Z_{\rho,\sigma}) of 'anchorings' of genus-1 Teichmüller-type groups compatible with scalar action \mu. That construction is not, to my knowledge, published in this form.
missed.quote: les formules (47) se réduisent à (50) \zeta\rho(\zeta)\rho^2(\zeta)=1, \eta_0\sigma(\eta_0)=1 ... On a donc bien construit un hom u_{G_4^+}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with explicit descriptions of Galois/GT actions on profinite SL_2(Z) and on genus-1 braid/Teichmüller groups. The value is mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck's concrete computations in genus 1.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine verification that twisted generators keep their orders (norm/cocycle conditions), plus the start of a sanity check. The surrounding project has some historical interest, but nothing here is a new result.
transcription_corrections: \zeta on this page is the same element written \xi on the next page and x on the previous page.
'u_{G_0}(\lambda_0)=[-...-]\mu\lambda_0' has a struck-out symbol before \mu; the intended formula is u(\lambda_0)=\mu\lambda_0.
The right-hand side of (1+\rho_M+\rho_M^2)= ... is 0_M after a crossed-out attempt.
